# path.py

[简体中文](path.zh.md) ｜ **English** ｜ [← Back to README](../../README.en.md)

PathElement: move / line / curve / arc commands, turtle drawing and boolean operations.

Path commands map one-to-one onto SVG path `d` syntax: move / line / horizontal and
vertical lines / quadratic and cubic Beziers / arc / close. It also supports boolean
operations, transforms, smoothing and turtle-style turning (forward, turn, rounded
corners).

---

## Classes and methods

### `PathElement`

Path element.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `get_d()` | Return the path's d string. |
| `set_d(d)` | Set the SVG path d string directly. |
| `move_to(x, y=None)` | Lift the pen, move to a point without drawing, and start a new subpath. |
| `line_to(end_x, end_y=None)` | Draw a straight line from the current point to the target point. |
| `h_line_to(end_x)` | Draw a horizontal line to end_x. |
| `v_line_to(end_y)` | Draw a vertical line to end_y. |
| `cubic_to(ctrl1, ctrl2, end)` | Cubic Bézier curve. |
| `smooth_cubic_to(ctrl2, end)` | Smooth cubic Bézier continuation. |
| `quad_to(ctrl, end)` | Quadratic Bézier curve. |
| `smooth_quad_to(end)` | Smooth quadratic Bézier continuation. |
| `ellipse_arc_to(rx, ry, end, sweep=0, large_arc=False, x_axis_rotation=0)` | Elliptical arc. |
| `arc_to(radius, end, sweep=0, large_arc=False)` | Circular arc. |
| `circle_to(center, sweep=0)` | Draw a full circle in the path using arc commands. |
| `close()` | Close the current subpath. |
| `new_subpath(x=None, y=None, **kw)` | Start a new subpath so one element can hold several disconnected pieces. |
| `forward(length)` | Move forward along the current heading, drawing a line. |
| `backward(length)` | Move backwards along the current heading, drawing a line. |
| `turn_right_move(angle, distance=0)` | Turn right by angle degrees and move without drawing. |
| `turn_left_move(angle, distance=0)` | Turn left by angle degrees and move without drawing. |
| `turn_right_line(angle, length)` | Turn right by angle degrees and draw a line. |
| `turn_left_line(angle, length)` | Turn left by angle degrees and draw a line. |
| `turn_right_arc(angle, radius)` | Turn-right arc: draw an arc curving to the right. |
| `turn_left_arc(angle, radius)` | Turn-left arc. |
| `fillet(p1, p2, radius)` | Round the corner between two segments: go from the current point through p1 towards p2 with an arc of radius. |
| `translate_cmds(dx, dy)` | Translate every coordinate of the path. |
| `reverse()` | Reverse the path direction, swapping start and end while keeping the shape. |
| `merge(other)` | Merge another path into this one. |
| `union(other)` | Union: return a new path element. |
| `intersect(other)` | Intersection. |
| `subtract(other)` | Difference. |
| `to_point_list(samples=200)` | Sample the path into a vertex list for boolean ops and measurements. |
| `length(samples=48)` | Total path length. |
| `point_at(ratio)` | Return the coordinates at a given fraction along the path. |
| `bbox()` | Path bounding box, approximated from sampled vertices. |
| `editor(refresh=False)` | Get a PathEditor for this path so you can inspect and drag its anchors and control points. |
| `segments()` | Return every PathSegment, each carrying its start, end and control points. |
| `anchors()` | Return every anchor point: the curve start, end and corner points. |
| `controls()` | Return every control point, i.e. the Bézier handles. |
| `anchor_points()` | Return every anchor coordinate as plain tuples, handy for printing or passing around. |
| `control_points()` | Return all control-point coordinates as plain tuples. |
| `move_anchor(index, x, y)` | Move the anchor at index and apply it immediately. |
| `move_control(seg_index, ctrl_index, x, y)` | Move control point ctrl_index of segment seg_index and apply it immediately. |
| `describe()` | Build a readable path report: start / controls / end per segment, plus every anchor. |
| `print_points()` | Print the path report so you can see how many points a curve has and where they sit. |
| `show_points(board=None, **kw)` | Draw anchors as squares and handles as lines with round dots, just like a pen tool. |
| `smooth(tightness=1.0)` | Smooth the polyline vertices into a Bézier curve. |

## Full example

Run it directly in PyCharm, or from the command line: `python malight/elements/path.py`

```python
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import os

    from malight import Malight, ColorName, FillRule
    from malight.pathkit import PathEditor

    _out = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__),
                                        "..", "..", "output"))
    pen = Malight(os.path.join(_out, "demo_path"), width=660, height=420)
    pen.set_background_color(ColorName.WHITESMOKE)

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1) Command-style drawing: move, line, Bezier, arc, close
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    p = pen.path(fill_color="none", stroke_color=ColorName.TOMATO,
                 stroke_width=3)
    p.move_to(60, 320)                                  # start
    p.line_to(140, 180)                                 # line
    p.cubic_to((200, 80), (300, 80), (360, 180))        # cubic Bezier, two control points
    p.quad_to((420, 240), (480, 180))                   # quadratic Bezier, one control point
    p.arc_to(40, (560, 240), sweep=1)                   # arc

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2) Inspect the structure: every segment's start, control and end point prints
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    print(p.describe())          # The point inspection the original edition's path element offered

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3) Edit: drag anchors and control points, written back to the path at once
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    print("anchors:", p.anchor_points())        # every anchor coordinate
    print("control points:", p.control_points())     # every Bezier handle coordinate
    print("segments with control points:", p.editor().curve_indices())   # line segments have no control points
    p.anchors()[2].move_to(200, 90)          # drag the third anchor
    p.controls()[0].move_by(0, -20)          # drag the first control point
    p.move_anchor(1, 150, 200)               # or address it by index
    p.move_control(2, 0, 210, 100)           # the first handle of segment 2, a cubic

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4) Structure edits: insert a point without changing the shape, reverse, save points
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    ed = p.editor()                          # the same as PathEditor(p)
    ed.insert_anchor(1, 0.5)                 # insert an anchor at the middle of segment 1, shape unchanged
    ed.reverse()                             # swap start and end
    ed.save_json(os.path.join(_out, "path_points.json"))   # save the points

    # 5) Visualise: anchors as squares, handles as lines with dots
    p.show_points(labels=True)

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6) Geometry: length, point at arc length, bounding box, translate every command
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    _len = p.length()
    print("path length ≈ %.2f" % (_len, _len))
    print("point at 30%% of arc length:", tuple(round(v, 2) for v in p.point_at(0.3)))
    print("bounding box:", tuple(round(v, 1) for v in p.bbox()))

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 7) More commands: horizontal and vertical lines, full circle, smooth joins
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    q = pen.path(fill_color="none", stroke_color=ColorName.STEELBLUE,
                 stroke_width=3)
    q.move_to(60, 380)
    q.h_line_to(200)                 # horizontal line
    q.v_line_to(350)                 # vertical line
    pen.text(280, 400, "h_line_to / v_line_to", font_size=13,
             fill_color=ColorName.DIMGRAY, h_align="middle")

    ring = pen.path(fill_color="none", stroke_color=ColorName.SEAGREEN,
                    stroke_width=3)
    ring.move_to(560, 340)           # fix one point first: the radius is its distance to the centre
    ring.circle_to((560, 385))       # draw the full circle

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 8) Fill rule: EVENODD punches holes using several subpaths in one path
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    ring2 = pen.path(fill_color=ColorName.TEAL, fill_rule=FillRule.EVENODD,
                     stroke_color="none")
    ring2.move_to(490, 60)
    ring2.circle_to((490, 105))      # outer ring, radius 45
    ring2.new_subpath(490, 75)       # a new subpath starts the inner ring
    ring2.circle_to((490, 105))      # inner ring, radius 30: EVENODD turns it into a hole

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 9) Boolean ops (union, intersection, difference) return a new PathElement
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    a = pen.path(fill_color="none", stroke_color=ColorName.NAVY)
    a.move_to(100, 60)
    a.circle_to((130, 90))
    b = pen.path(fill_color="none", stroke_color=ColorName.CRIMSON)
    b.move_to(150, 60)
    b.circle_to((130, 90))
    try:
        merged = a.union(b)
        print("union result d length:", len(merged.get_d()))
    except Exception as exc:                 # requires optional dependencies such as shapely
        print("boolean ops need an optional dependency, skipping:", type(exc).__name__)

    pen.finish()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bottom import: show_points()'s return annotation names GroupElement, which subclasses
# the Element defined here - a top-level import would cycle; the bottom solves both.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
from .group import GroupElement  # noqa: E402
```
